kicker: Music labels · Q2 FY27 · catalogue economics
title: Old songs pay; the paywall is the lever
dek: Tips and Saregama grew Q2 FY27 revenue 35% and 37%, mostly on more streams: YouTube still pays Tips about ₹0.05 a stream. Only about 3% of Indian listeners pay for music, against 57% in the US.

read: The catalogues already earn like annuities; with per-stream rates flat, faster growth now depends on Indian listeners moving to paid tiers.
sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and Q1–Q2 FY27 earnings calls of Tips Music and Saregama; IFPI
notes: Revenue growth is from filed Q2 FY27 results: Tips (standalone) ₹120 cr, +35%, profit +24%; Saregama (consolidated) ₹314 cr, +37%, with music revenue ₹251 cr, +35%. Tips' EBITDA margin was 70.5% vs 76% a year earlier because content cost nearly doubled; Saregama's music EBITDA of ₹154 cr is 61% of music revenue, against about 60% a year ago. The 85% catalogue share, ≈₹0.05 per-stream rate and 10–15% subscription share come from Tips' Q2 call; the 40–50% subscriber growth from its Q1 call. Penetration figures are third-party estimates cited by Saregama management on its Q1 FY27 call and are indicative only. Saregama also cites IFPI data putting India at about 1% of the US$31.7 bn global recorded-music market in 2025.
